title: Resting-heart-rate reserve features did not establish improved cross-center coronary disease prediction
abstract: Resting heart rate is omitted from the conventional UCI heart-disease subset but available in the raw records. We tested established reserve-based exercise physiology representations using 293 Hungarian patients for training and 143 eligible Long Beach VA patients for independent-center confirmation. Adding resting heart rate, achieved chronotropic reserve and reserve-adjusted ST depression changed frozen Brier loss from 0.20407 to 0.19678 (difference -0.00729, paired patient bootstrap 95% interval -0.01580 to +0.00118), without improved discrimination (AUROC 0.72360 to 0.71327). Increment beyond resting heart rate alone was -0.00162 (-0.00524 to +0.00197). A flexible additive comparator and exploratory target-intercept calibration did not support a reserve-specific advantage. The result is inconclusive for incremental prediction and does not negate the established physiological value of chronotropic assessment. Complete-case selection, medication/protocol confounding and marked site shifts limit interpretation.
